However, the error occurs because the mean function tries to compute a mean of numeric_only columns that include both float64 and int64 dtypes, which is not allowed according to the rule 'safe'.

Following the execution path, we find that `pandas.core.groupby.generic.GenericGroupBy.mean()` attempts to compute the mean using `_cython_agg_general` method, which ultimately fails due to the TypeError raised when trying to safely cast non-equivalent float64 to int64.

The issue can be traced back to line 1223 in `pandas/core/groupby/generic.py`, where the return statement calls `self._cython_agg_general("mean", ...)`, which seems to be attempting to aggregate numeric-only columns without proper handling of mixed data types.

To fix this bug, consider adding a check for data type consistency within the 'numeric_only' columns before attempting aggregation. This can be done by ensuring that all columns in `numeric_only` are of the same dtype or raise an appropriate exception if they are not.

pandas.core.groupby.generic.GenericGroupBy.mean
